To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we were able to prepare new ferrocenyl sulfonium based ionic liquids, which show reversible redox potentials, low absorbance in visible light and are therefore promising for applications as redox mediatiors in dye sensitized cells, as redox electrolyte in supercapacitor or as overcharge additives in batteries.
the redox chemistry of ferrocenyl sulfonium salts is strongly influenced by the cation-anion interaction in the solid and the redox potential can be tuned in a broad range.
we have synthesized and characterized new ferrocenyl sulfonium based ionic liquids and studied their redox behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of novel organometallic ILs based on ferrocenyl sulfonium salts.
the synthesis, characterization and application of new ferrocene based ionic liquids.
the synthesis of new organometallic ionic liquids based on ferrocenylthioether derivatives and their characterization by cyclic voltammetry, UV/Vis-spectroscopy and thermoanalytical measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ferrocenium cation is not only a redox-active center but also an excellent platform for further functionalization.
ferrocenyl sulfonium based ionic liquids are a new class of redox active ionic liquids, which are highly promising for future applications in electrochemistry.
the redox activity of ferrocenyl based sulfonium cations is not significantly influenced by the presence of a bis(trifluoro-methanesulfonylimide) (TFSI-) anion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ferrocenyl based sulfonium ILs are redox active, highly conductive and have a high thermal stability.
we have shown that the ferrocene based sulfonium cations can be easily synthesized, and that they can be used as redox mediates in DSSCs.
ferrocenyl sulfonium based ILs are a new class of redox active ILs, which are easily prepared by direct alkoxylation and which can be tuned in their redox potentials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redox potential of the ferrocenium cation can be tuned by the sulfonium group.
the sulfonium group can be directly bonded to the redox active ferrocenyl moiety and still be reversibly reduced.
the ferrocenium cation is an excellent candidate for a redox-active IL cation.
